blockers: Headline H1 'penalty' and H2 'confirmed' on the haiku union rest on a union that passes the pre-registered solve-rate gate only by averaging two sets that individually differ sharply. PREREGISTRATION.md says gates apply 'per model and set'; the arXiv replication set (79 of 103 problems, 77%) failed the gate (haiku solve 0.05; my recompute 4/78) and the paper itself says that set 'is not interpreted on its own' (main.tex:65). The union solve rate is 21/102=0.206, 0.006 above the 0.2 floor, which is a product of mixing a 0.71 set with a 0.05 set. Abstract (main.tex:19) and contribution (1) present the union result as the confirmatory finding without saying that three quarters of it comes from a gate-failed set. The properly gated subset (2026 contests, n=24) shows H1 D=0.00, 90% CI [-0.125,+0.125] (equivalence not shown, no penalty shown either).

H2 'confirmed' is carried by very few informative pools. Only 29 of 103 pools have any variation in the three isolated verdicts (the rest contribute exactly 0); of these 26 are arXiv-set and only 3 are in the gated 2026-contest set. Among informative pools the picked candidate beats the others in 21 and loses in 8. The 'same direction on the 2026 contests alone' (main.tex:71, p=0.043) therefore rests on 3 pools, and that p would not survive Holm over the 4 pre-registered tests (smallest-p threshold 0.0125). The text calling the effect 'confirmed' and 'a confirmed failure of forced selection' (main.tex:30) needs this scope stated.

The 'competence' account (no penalty where the judge solves, penalty where it cannot) is post hoc (F5, not in the C2 pre-registration) and is confounded by dataset. Solvability is almost perfectly collinear with source: of 108 unsolved problems 74 are the arXiv replication set (solved share 0.05), whereas solved problems are 34 screen and 16 contest items. Solvability is also measured with one SOLVE sample per problem, and the hypothesis was formed after the S1 null and C2 data were seen, on pooled S1+C2 data. The strata contrast I recompute is D(unsolved)=+0.120 [90% CI +0.046,+0.194; 95% +0.037,+0.213] vs D(solved)=-0.056 [-0.148,+0.037] (interaction +0.176, 95% bootstrap [+0.03,+0.32]), but it cannot separate 'beyond competence' from 'arXiv-derived items / longer candidates / different graders'. The abstract and conclusion (main.tex:19, 87) state it as the explanation ('the penalty appears beyond competence'); it should be labelled a hypothesis, and 'no penalty within competence' is also not an equivalence result (solved-stratum CI half-width is about 0.09-0.10 only at 90%, lower bound -0.148, outside the +/-0.10 margin used elsewhere).

Deviation from the pre-registered gate logic is not recorded in AMENDMENTS.md. The pre-registration lists the union as primary and gates per set, and the outcome section of AMENDMENTS.md reports 'haiku union (gate passed)' next to 'replication set: gate FAILED, not interpreted' without discussing that these conflict; no amendment states which governs when they disagree.
non_blocking: Unit of analysis is the problem (103 unique pids, one pool per problem) and the bootstrap resamples problems: correct. Clustering by competition is not modelled (arxivmath-0826 n=47 D=+0.128, arxivmath-0926 n=32 D=+0.188, hmmt n=18 D=0, aime n=6 D=0); with 4 competitions, between-competition variance is unaccounted for. The CIs are a within-sample bootstrap and are probably optimistic for generalisation to new item sets.

H1 discordance on the union is 18 (PICK chose, ISO accepted none) vs 6 (reverse); exact McNemar two-sided p about 0.023. The 'directional fallback' p=0.007 is one-sided and outside the 4-test Holm family; it is a fallback that was allowed in the pre-registration but should be flagged as not multiplicity-adjusted. The headline Holm number for H1 (0.62) is a TOST p, which is correct, but the abstract narrative of a 'penalty' leans on the unadjusted fallback.

ISO-any uses three independent isolated calls (max over 3) versus a single PICK call, so the arms differ in number of draws; this makes ISO-any more liberal and works against H1 detecting a penalty, but the contrast is a format-and-count package, not a pure presentation effect. Single-sample per arm, no repeated runs for call noise.

Sonnet gate failed on ISO parse 0.896 (10 of 96 unparsed) vs 0.90, a miss of 0.004; the H1 sample then drops to 17 of 24 problems by listwise deletion of unparsed ISO verdicts (my recompute n=17, D=0.00, 90% CI [-0.118,+0.118]). Missingness is not random with respect to difficulty. The pre-registered sonnet cost cap of 12 USD was exceeded (29.10 USD, D3); disclosed.

Candidate-level ISO false-accept rate on wrong candidates is 0.149 in C2 (S1: 0.111); accept of right candidates 0.54 on 100 parsed, so the discrimination gate (>=0.10) passes comfortably (0.39). The pre-registered power calculation (90% CI half-width about 0.073) matches the realised half-width of 0.078.

AMENDMENTS.md D2 correction cites 'analysis/posthoc/solvability_split.json'; the file is at exps/posthoc/solvability_split.json. The PREREGISTRATION.md header time (23:30 UTC) is later than the commit time (6bdfeee, 23:24:35); the earliest raw file mtime is 23:25:07, so ordering is plausible but the stated time is not exact.

Seventeen tournament hypotheses are 'not yet tested' and 17 more 'killed before data', so the 61 is not the number of tests run; about 10 screens with 95% CIs are reported with no correction but are labelled exploratory. My simple answer-equivalence grader (string and fraction normalisation) gives slightly different SOLVE counts than the paper's mathgrade (S1 0.567 vs 0.60; C2 conf 0.667 vs 0.71; C2 repl 0.051 vs 0.05), so strata sizes I get are 54/108 vs the paper's 57/105. Conclusions do not change.
